title: Frame and steering fundamentals
summary: Understand the structural frame, steering fork, stem and headset as one connected control system.

steps.title: The frame locates the bicycle's major systems.
steps.body: The frame holds the wheels, crank, saddle and steering assembly in defined geometric relationships while carrying rider and road loads.
steps.keyFact: Frame geometry changes handling because it changes where those systems are positioned relative to each other.

steps.title: The fork holds the front wheel and steers it.
steps.body: The fork connects the front wheel to the steering axis. Turning the handlebar rotates the fork around that axis.
steps.keyFact: The fork is both a structural wheel support and part of the steering mechanism.

steps.title: The headset lets the fork rotate in the frame.
steps.body: The headset is a bearing assembly around the steering axis. It carries steering loads while allowing smooth rotation between fork and frame.
steps.keyFact: Too loose produces play; too tight or damaged bearings make steering rough.

steps.title: Find the steering bearing.
steps.body: Identify the component that sits at the steering axis and allows fork rotation relative to the frame.
steps.keyFact: The headset is the steering bearing system.

challenge.prompt: Which component is the steering bearing assembly?
challenge.successText: Correct. The headset is the bearing system between frame and fork.
challenge.retryText: That component is part of steering, but it is not the bearing assembly.
